rationales.authenticity: The framing of folk medicine against church authority is historically apt; 'willow bark and a steady hand' as a rejoinder to sermon-preaching is period-authentic.
rationales.character: 'The Father sees the world through the lens of the pulpit rather than the reality of the hearth' is a sharp, character-revealing line that positions Brigid as pragmatic and quietly independent.
rationales.craft: The dialogue has two strong, linked sentences and a memorable closing image; the JSON metadata block again adds unwanted length, but the core is the strongest in this batch.
rationales.language: Clear English with one Irish phrase correctly used; well-formed prose; no non-Latin script.
rationales.responsiveness: Directly engages with the priest's sermon and offers a pointed personal view, which is the most engaged response in the set.
